content.title: ABC
content.text: Sadly, Conan, whom I love, will misuse the word film. As long as major institutions continue to push the word “film,” confusion about the medium will continue. When events like the Oscars present modern productions as “film” and call digital creators “filmmakers,” they reinforce language that no longer matches the technology being used. That repetition shapes public understanding, and when inaccurate terminology is repeated by authoritative organizations, it becomes normalized whether it is correct or not. Film is a specific medium. It is photochemical emulsion exposed to light and transported through a film camera. Digital video is a different technology built on electronic sensors, signal processing, codecs, and solid state storage. The tools, workflows, and engineering behind these systems are not the same. When everything is labeled “film,” the distinction disappears and the public loses the ability to understand how modern productions are actually created. Knowing the difference is also about respect. More than a century of engineers, technicians, and skilled professionals worked behind the scenes to move motion picture technology from mechanical and chemical systems into the electronic imaging tools we use today. Sensors, digital processing, compression systems, storage media, and modern editing pipelines did not appear by accident. They were built by generations of innovators whose work deserves to be recognized accurately. Clear language would solve much of this. Terms like movie production, screen production, or digital video production describe the work without attaching it to a technology that is rarely used today. Accuracy does not diminish the legacy of film. It acknowledges both histories and respects the people who built the tools that power modern production. Respect for the past means knowing what film was. Respect for the present means accurately representing digital video and the people who use it today. We make movies and not all movies are films, especially in the 21st century.
